title: Privacy Policy Compliance Judgment
description: The single JSON object judge/pipeline.py emits for one full privacy-policy text: every segmented clause, one judge verdict per (clause, retrieved-reference) pair, and a policy-level aggregation of those verdicts per GDPR article. This is the stable contract downstream scoring/UI code is built against -- see judge/pipeline.py's module docstring for how each section is produced.

meta.description: Provenance for this run: when it ran and which judge model / retrieval configuration produced it.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp the pipeline finished at.

config.description: Path to the judge/config/qlora_judge*.yaml used (picks the base Qwen model + generation settings).

adapter.description: Path to the fine-tuned LoRA adapter directory loaded on top of the base model.

source.description: Path (or "<inline>") the policy text was read from.

clauses.description: The clause-segmented policy text, in document order.

clause_verdicts.description: One entry per (clause, retrieved-reference) pair actually judged -- up to `meta.retrieval.k` entries per clause. A `gdpr_concept` chunk (see rag/parsers/gdpr.py) covers two articles at once, so its single judge call produces one entry per article it links, sharing the same `chunk_id`.

articles.description: One entry per GDPR article known to the RAG index (see judge/pipeline.py's `known_articles`), aggregating every clause_verdicts entry with that article_number. Includes articles no clause ever retrieved, flagged `not_addressed`.

compliance_status.description: Mirrors judge/judge_schema.json's `compliance_status`, plus `needs_review`: the pipeline's own fallback (never a judge output) for a clause/article the judge could not produce a schema-valid verdict for even after one repair retry -- see `error`/`retry_used` below.

article.description: Human-readable label for what was retrieved, e.g. "13", "concept:6,21", "Recital 47", or an EDPB guideline section heading.

article_number.description: Base GDPR article number this entry aggregates under in `articles[]`; null for a retrieved recital or EDPB guideline chunk (source_type != gdpr_article/gdpr_concept), which is judged for evidence but isn't itself a GDPR article.

chunk_id.description: The retrieved chunk's id in the Chroma collection.

retrieval_rank.description: 1-based rank within this clause's top-k retrieval results.

retrieval_score.description: rag.retriever.RetrievedChunk.score for this (clause, chunk) pair; not comparable across clauses using different retrieval modes.

retry_used.description: True if the first judge generation was invalid JSON and the one repair retry (or its own failure) produced this entry.

error.description: Schema-validation error text when compliance_status is needs_review; null otherwise.

clauses_addressing_it.description: Every clause_verdicts entry whose article_number is this article, regardless of its compliance_status (including not_applicable). Empty exactly when best_compliance_status is not_addressed.

best_compliance_status.description: not_addressed means no clause in the policy ever retrieved this article (clauses_addressing_it is empty) -- distinct from not_applicable, where at least one clause was checked against the article and the judge determined it doesn't apply. Otherwise the most favorable status among clauses_addressing_it, ranked compliant > partial > not_applicable > needs_review > non_compliant (see judge/pipeline.py's _STATUS_RANK) -- a convenience default; a scoring engine that wants a different rule can recompute one from the full clauses_addressing_it list.

evidence.description: evidence_span of the clause that produced best_compliance_status; empty for not_addressed.

rationale.description: rationale of the clause that produced best_compliance_status; a fixed explanatory string for not_addressed.
